data.why: The repository ships no real SEM micrograph (its test images are named in a git-ignored tests/local_data.json and not bundled); a grayscale photo with distinct round edges lets the agent exercise contour tracing, edge snapping, rulers, angles and line profiles after entering a pixel size by hand.

goals: calibrate the pixel scale by entering the pixel width and height so lengths read out in micrometres
trace a polygon contour around a feature and read off its perimeter, area and bounding box
measure a distance with the ruler tool and an angle at a vertex or between two lines
take a line profile across an edge, averaged across a band, and check that it squares to the edge it crosses
place markers A and B on a profile to measure an edge-to-edge distance
export the measurements as a CSV file, a contour as a polygon or GDSII file, and save the whole session

review.summary: This tree is accurate and well layered. Its goal and three phases match the README's open → calibrate → trace and measure → keep and export workflow, and the screens I opened support nearly every node. It needs small fixes before filing: give snapping and display tasks to the features that already cover them, add the metadata-calibration route as an unreached branch, and correct two loosely cited screens (019, 042).
